custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154789-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154789-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens with a green "Active" pill.

Step 2:

  • Inactive is picked, and nothing is applied yet: the pill still reads a green "Active".

Step 3:

  • Before anything changes, a confirmation titled "Deactivate part?" opens over the part window.
  • It is the app's standard confirmation: a title with a close X at its right, message lines, a "Note (Optional)" field, Cancel and a red Deactivate button, and there is no word to type to confirm.

Step 4:

  • The confirmation closes.

Step 5:

  • The window closes and part A is still on the Active tab.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S10-R1: “A status change is confirmed before it is applied, from either entry point: the bulk bar (Stories 2 and 3), or Save in the part dialog after the user picks a different Part Status (S13-R21).”
  • S10-R2: “The confirmation is the application's standard confirmation dialog. There is no confirmation word to type.”
  • S13-R21: “Picking a different status changes nothing until Save. When Save is pressed with a different status picked, the confirmation of Story 10 opens first.”
  • Key Decisions: “Every confirmation is the application's standard dialog. A title with the close X, a message, an optional note, Cancel and a confirm button. There is no confirmation word to type.”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "3.3 Save asks first". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • retire-03-p3-3-confirm.png

The design's own words:

  • “Save raises "Deactivate part?" (S10-R1, S10-R3). It opens with the part number and description (S10-R4), then the three lines of S10-R6, then the optional note (S10-R10). The note here reads "Superseded by N6801-06-04X". The red Deactivate button has Cancel to its left (S10-R11). The bulk confirmation (board 4.4) is the same dialog, built from the design system Modal and Button.”
